hypothesis: A learned row-stochastic role-to-entity transition operator, composed along ordered and inverse typed paths, carries more useful uncertainty about variable bindings than any matched hard inferred grammar, and generalizes to new relational structures.
source: New project-authored synthetic development generator: directed affine/cyclic and random bijective role graphs; anonymized entity IDs; public noisy triples (role, subject, object); held-out ordered query with forward/reverse inverse roles. Public demonstrations cannot include a queried answer directly; adversarial same-topology role reordering.
learned: Per-episode SGD on public transition triple likelihood; soft row-wise transition probabilities, q8 quantized 8x8x8, probability message passing for role-ordered forward/inverse edges. No private grammar inputs.
